scope: Original fixed pixel drawings; optional data-only Workshop pack. Labels are editorial candidates, not calibrated human difficulty.

studies.title: The filigree lantern
studies.story: The narrow handle, separated brass frame and pierced flame are three different silhouettes. Reconstruct their shared rows without assuming bilateral symmetry.
studies.editorialFocus: Separate the two edge-frame runs from the central flame. Completing a long lower bar constrains the interrupted columns above it.

studies.title: The slit in the dome
studies.story: A dark observatory dome has a slit, two lower windows and an off-centre sighting vane. Empty squares distinguish the openings from the shell.
studies.editorialFocus: The long equator overlaps first, but the roof slit interrupts its columns. Compare the two window gaps against the displaced vane instead of mirroring the roof.

studies.title: The last river skiff
studies.story: Two unequal sails share a mast above a layered hull. The broken waterline belongs to neither sail.
studies.editorialFocus: Work from the hull overlaps into the mast columns. The two sail triangles have different extents; copying one into the other makes the row counts fail.

studies.title: Two stairwell windows
studies.story: Two hollow windows sit on opposite sides of a staircase. Their dark frames and the stair treads must be separated by the column clues.
studies.editorialFocus: The repeated tread pairs align differently as the steps climb. Use the hollow window columns to distinguish a tread extension from a window edge.

studies.title: The alternating herb
studies.story: Alternating leaves grow from a narrow stem over a stepped pot. The tip bends away from the main stalk.
studies.editorialFocus: The pot rim anchors its columns, while the left and right leaf masses start on different rows. Keep the gaps where separate leaves touch a shared column.

studies.title: The reader at dusk
studies.story: An articulated desk lamp bends above an open book. Two short light marks stand apart from its arm.
studies.editorialFocus: The broad shade overlaps and the split book base constrain different columns. Keep the arm diagonal separate from the two short light marks.

studies.title: The cabinet moth
studies.story: Two carved moth wings surround a segmented body. Their holes are deliberately different, so symmetry is not a solving rule.
studies.editorialFocus: The central body anchors several dense rows, but the wing holes interrupt different columns. Cross-check the upper paired runs before completing either wing.

studies.title: The tilted orrery
studies.story: A tilted orbital frame passes through a central sphere and rests on a short plinth. The tilt breaks the circular outline.
studies.editorialFocus: The diagonal and ring share some filled squares without becoming one run everywhere. Use plinth columns to separate lower arc segments from the supporting stem.

studies.title: The narrow hourglass
studies.story: Two bowls narrow to a single throat between heavy horizontal end plates. Open spaces inside the bowls have different shapes.
studies.editorialFocus: The paired end plates give long overlaps, but the upper and lower internal gaps are not mirror copies. Carry the throat columns through each bowl separately.

studies.title: The twin-window kettle
studies.story: A kettle with two small inset windows has a side spout, a thin handle and a detached shelf below it.
studies.editorialFocus: Use the shelf and body overlaps to locate the two interior gaps. The narrow handle extends farther than the body and must remain separate from the spout.
